title: Merging Strategies & Conflict Resolution
description: Combine lines of development with fast-forward and three-way merges, decipher conflict markers, and resolve collisions cleanly.

blocks.content:
## Integrating Branches with `git merge`

When work on a branch is finished, you integrate it into the target branch (usually `main`) using `git merge`:

```bash
# 1. Switch to the receiving branch
git switch main

# 2. Merge the incoming feature branch
git merge feature-login
```

Git analyzes the commit history to determine which merge strategy to apply.

## Fast-Forward vs Three-Way Merges

### 1. Fast-Forward Merge

If the target branch has not received any new commits since the feature branch diverged, Git simply moves the pointer forward. No new merge commit is created.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Before [Before Merge]
        A["C1"] --> B["C2 (main)"]
        B --> C["C3"]
        C --> D["C4 (feature)"]
    end
    subgraph After [After Fast-Forward Merge]
        A2["C1"] --> B2["C2"]
        B2 --> C2["C3"]
        C2 --> D2["C4 (main, feature)"]
    end
```

### 2. Three-Way Merge (True Merge)

If both branches have progressed with independent commits, a fast-forward is impossible. Git identifies the Common Ancestor commit, creates a synthetic 3-way diff, and creates a **Merge Commit** with two parent pointers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C1["C1"] --> C2["C2 (Base)"]
    C2 --> C3["C3 (main)"]
    C2 --> C4["C4 (feature)"]
    C3 --> M["M (Merge Commit)"]
    C4 --> M
```

## Anatomy of a Merge Conflict

A merge conflict occurs when both branches modify the exact same lines of a file differently, or when one branch deletes a file that another modified. Git halts the merge and inserts conflict markers:

```text
<<<<<<< HEAD (Current branch: main)
const API_BASE_URL = "https://api.production.internal";
=======
const API_BASE_URL = "https://api.staging.internal";
>>>>>>> feature-login (Incoming branch)
```

- `<<<<<<< HEAD`: Marks the start of changes from your current branch.
- `=======`: The divider separating the two competing versions.
- `>>>>>>> <branch-name>`: Marks the end of incoming changes from the merged branch.

## Step-by-Step Conflict Resolution

1. Run `git status` to see all files marked `both modified`.
2. Open the conflicting files in your editor. Choose which lines to keep, combine, or rewrite.
3. Delete the conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`).
4. Stage the resolved files with `git add <file>`.
5. Finalize the merge commit:

```bash
git commit -m "merge: resolve API base URL conflict between main and feature-login"
```

If something goes wrong and you want to cancel the merge entirely:

```bash
git merge --abort
```

blocks.question: When does Git perform a fast-forward merge instead of creating a three-way merge commit?
options: When the incoming branch has zero commits
When no new commits have occurred on the target branch since divergence
When merging via remote pull requests only
blocks.explanation: If the destination branch history has not progressed since the feature branched off, Git simply slides the pointer forward to the tip of the incoming branch.

blocks.question: Which command cancels an in-progress merge and restores your files to the state prior to calling git merge?
blocks.explanation: 'git merge --abort' cleanly terminates an incomplete merge process and returns the working tree and index to their pre-merge condition.
